ann_81.text: In this straight-line part, an international plan clearly raises the predicted chance for a typical customer from about 2% to about 17%.
More voice-mail messages raise it steadily, from about 2% at 0 messages to about 10% at 32 messages, and being in Washington raises it to about 8% (on the training data only).
A voice-mail plan lowers it only slightly.

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted chance only slightly (on the training data only): more international minutes and more night-time minutes raise it steadily; more international calls lower it steadily, each extra call taking off about the same; a higher night-time charge also lowers it steadily; and Montana, Maine and the other states and area code 510 shift it by a few points at most.

More daytime minutes raise it only slightly here, in an uneven way across customers (on the training data only).
More daytime minutes clearly raise it, in an uneven way across customers, and even more so outside Oregon and Alaska (about 1% to 15%, against below 1% to 2% in Oregon).

Per-category logit shift (weight x z-span): internationalPlan +2.57 (380 rows, churn 0.42), voiceMailPlan -0.98/sd partly offset by numberVmailMessages +0.80/sd; intl minutes +0.41/sd, intl calls -0.26/sd; night minutes +0.163 and night charge -0.015 are the same column after z-scoring (max diff 0.002), net +0.148/sd. State offsets from ~56-86 rows each: state:11 -2.02, state:46 -1.83, state:5 -1.22, state:47 +1.13, state:26 +0.94, state:21 +0.65, state:38 -0.64, state:14 -0.52, state:18 +0.50 (raw empirical log-odds -0.42: sign opposite), state:36 -0.34 (raw +0.30). Mean-ablation on train: AUC 0.911 -> 0.816.

ann_82.original:
Customer-service-calls threshold: direct CSC slope plus relu 1255 that cancels it for few calls and releases it from about 3-4 calls; state 37 switches the relu off.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Customer-service-calls threshold. Term = 1.619*CSC + 2.792*relu(0.008 - 0.55*CSC + 0.292*dayMinutes - 2.646*state37 - 0.036*state0). While 1255 is on the CSC slope nearly cancels (1.619 - 2.792*0.55 = +0.08/sd). Train, mean term by calls 0..6: 0.94, 1.06, 1.19, 1.89, 3.02, 4.25, 5.49; 1255 on in 98/96/72/25/3/0% of rows. Train churn: 0-3 calls 0.11, 4 calls 0.44, 5 0.57, 6 0.68. Threshold sits between 3 and 4 calls (sharper than at generation 100); +0.29*dayMinutes delays the release for heavy day users. State 37 (84 rows, z 6.8) forces 1255 off, so for those rows CSC is linear throughout: logit -1.56 on their 62 rows with 0-2 calls (model predicts 0.048 vs observed 0.113; without the switch 0.112), ~0 at 4+ calls. ann_82.proposed: Customer-service calls raise the predicted chance slightly; the rise with daytime minutes is much smaller for customers in Oregon.

ann_83.original:
Day-charge hinges 216 and 4311, gate 3384 (state 42 / eve charge, suppressed by 216 and 6468), and the always-on state-39 unit 6468 (affine offset).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Three exits. 216 = relu(-0.328 + 0.222*dayCharge - 0.74*state22) (w 1.582) is a second high-day hinge (dayCharge equals dayMinutes after z-scoring, max diff 5e-4): +0.25 logit in the top day decile, forced off in state 22. 3384 = relu(-1.274 + 1.018*state42 + 0.698*eveCharge - 1.163*216 - 0.577*6468) fires for exactly the 68 state-42 rows (6468 >= 2.28 always), and feeds 4311 = relu(-0.295 + 0.243*dayCharge + 0.788*3384) (w -0.057): a -0.22 logit state-42 offset (net state-42 effect with its +0.44 direct edge ~ +0.22). 6468 = relu(2.297 + 0.118*state39) is always on (min pre-activation 2.28): exact affine state-39 offset, -0.97 logit on 82 rows (churn 0.061). Logit sd 0.17, linear R2 0.83. Train AUC: mean-ablated or linearised ~0.000 change; restoring alone onto all-linear +0.007 (the 216 hinge).
ann_83.proposed: Small effects of daytime charge above about $39.87 and of evening charge.

ann_84.original:
26442 = relu(0.50 - 0.88 dayCharge + 0.98*595), 595 = low-intl-charge hinge: lowers churn logit... preliminary, to be quantified.

Evidence (train, n=4000): 26442 = relu(0.497 - 0.883*dayCharge + 0.979*595), 595 = relu(-0.556 - 0.817*intlCharge - 0.653*relu(0.342 + 0.991*intlCharge)), w 0.978. 595 is a low-intl-charge hinge: on for 100% of the lowest intl quintile (mean 0.60), 23% of the 2nd, 0 above. 26442 is a LOW-day-usage hinge: mean logit term by day decile 2.14, 1.48, 1.19, 0.91, 0.70, 0.48, 0.28, 0.12, 0.04, 0.02, with low intl charge adding ~+0.3 in the low/mid day tertiles. Train churn by day decile 0.10, 0.165, 0.075, 0.11, 0.09, 0.06, 0.065, 0.08, 0.17, 0.49: it makes the day-usage response U-shaped together with the high-usage hinges. Linear R2 0.83. Train AUC: mean-ablated 0.911 -> 0.899; but its best linear fit (a straight negative day slope) gives 0.913, slightly ABOVE the full model, so its kink adds nothing to train ranking given the other hinges; restored alone onto the all-linear model it adds +0.017 (it supplies a day slope the linear backbone lacks).
ann_84.proposed: A higher daytime charge lowers the predicted chance while it stays below about $35.84.

ann_85.original:
High day+evening usage hinge 3227; 6038 adds an evening-minutes ramp gated by voicemail plan; the state-7 chain 5324->6316 feeds it with negligible weight.

Evidence (train, n=4000): High-usage hinge 4.251*relu(-1.625 + 0.848*dayMinutes + 0.095*eveMinutes + 0.927*relu(0.428 + 0.438*eveMinutes - 0.825*voiceMailPlan - 0.006*state30) + 0.007*6316). 6038 (inner relu) is on for 98% of no-voicemail rows and 3% of voicemail rows, so the evening slope is ~0.50 without a voicemail plan and 0.095 with one, and a voicemail plan lowers the hinge input by ~0.77 * 0.927. 6316 = relu(-1.09 + 0.672*relu(-0.404+0.722*state7)) fires only for state 7 (73 rows) and adds 0.065 logit: negligible. By day-minutes decile, hinge active 0/0/0/1/2/6/13/21/38/74%, mean logit term +0.67 in decile 9 and +2.47 in the top decile, where train churn is 0.49 (0.06-0.17 elsewhere). Linear R2 0.36. Train AUC: linearised 0.911 -> 0.882, mean-ablated -> 0.841; restoring it alone onto the all-linear model +0.060 (the largest single source).
ann_85.proposed: For customers with no voice-mail plan, high daytime and evening minutes together raise the predicted chance steeply; a voice-mail plan switches this off.

ann_86.original:
Always-on units 3930 (accountLength) and 20832 (state 7) are exact affine terms; 2698 (state 49) is never active on train (dead).

Evidence (train, n=4000): 3930 = relu(0.98 + 0.291*accountLength) is always on (min pre-activation 0.26): exact affine accountLength term, +0.077 logit per sd. 20832 = relu(2.121 + 0.898*state7) always on: exact state-7 offset, -1.10 logit on 73 rows (churn 0.082). 2698 = relu(-0.464 + 0.0315*state49): max pre-activation -0.29 on train, dead. Linear R2 1.0; AUC change under mean-ablation -0.0005.
ann_86.proposed: Small shifts for account length and Washington DC.

ann_87.original:
Root: P(churn)=sigmoid(-2.449 + sum of the six children's readouts). Purely additive in the logit: linear backbone + CSC threshold + day/eve usage hinge + day-charge hinges + low-day x low-intl interaction + affine offsets. 31 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Additive composition in the logit: P(churn)=sigmoid(-2.449 + linear_backbone + csc_threshold + 4.251*dayEveHinge + (1.582*216 - 0.057*4311 - 1.169*6468) + 0.978*lowDayHinge + (0.263*3930 - 0.164*20832 + 0.23*2698)). No child gates another; 31 unconnected inputs (26 states, area codes 408 and 415, day/eve/night call counts) have zero effect. Train AUC 0.9113 vs refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433 and the all-children-linearised network 0.8327. Restoring one child's nonlinearity onto the all-linear model: linear_backbone +0.0, csc_threshold +0.0393, day_eve_hinge +0.0604, day_charge_cluster +0.0069, intl_lowday_interaction +0.0169, affine_offsets +0.0. Linearising only the three day-usage children jointly gives 0.872. The gain over linear (~0.079) comes from the high day/eve usage hinge and the 3-4 call CSC threshold; state one-hots all off costs 0.004 train AUC.
ann_87.proposed: The predicted chance that a customer leaves rises with an international plan and with daytime minutes, steeply above about 245 minutes and when evening minutes are high; voice-mail messages and state shift it; the numbers of daytime, evening and night-time calls are ignored.

More daytime minutes clearly raise it, in an uneven way across customers, from about 1% at 112 minutes to about 15% at 249 minutes, and even more so if evening minutes are above 201 (about 1% to 40%, against 1% to 4%).

More voice-mail messages raise it steadily, from about 2% at 0 messages to about 10% at 32 messages, and being in Washington instead of West Virginia raises it to about 8% (on the training data only).
A higher daytime charge lowers it slightly, lowest at about $37, higher either side, and going from 0 to 3 customer-service calls raises it slightly, slowly at first, then faster.
The model ignores the number of daytime, evening and night-time calls.
